findings.title: Mount effect and hook file well over the project size guides
findings.description: The mount effect runs 157 lines, against a guide of about 50 lines per function. The whole file is 366 lines, against about 300. The `eslint.config.js` suppression comment justifies itself by saying inlining the facade would leave the file "~60% over". The file is still about 22% over after the extraction. `teardown`, the mount sequence and the subscription setup could each be pulled into helpers. A `mountChart(container, style, …)` function returning `{ observer, disposers }` would also make the `let observer` / `const disposers` hoisting, which `teardown` reads before it is declared, unnecessary.

findings.title: Visible-range translation is gated on a ref, so it cannot react to the first series being added
findings.description: The effect reads `seriesCountRef.current` but lists only `[mount.ready, chart, range]` as dependencies. A ref change does not re-run the effect. When a series is added to an empty chart, the Context's current range is not applied. It only reaches the chart on the next `range` change. The test "applies the range once a series exists" avoids this by calling `setRange` after `addSeries`, so it never covers the case. The comment calls this a seam for initiative 120. Even so, the first add leaves the chart and the Context out of sync. Either apply the range inside the facade's `addSeries` path when the count goes 0→1, or track the count as state.

findings.title: Subscriptions and the indicator effect are no-ops, and the teardown-race test is vacuous
findings.description: The crosshair and visible-range handlers contain only `if (disposedRef.current) { return }`, so both branches do nothing. The adapter still builds a crosshair payload on every mouse move for no consumer. The indicator effect at lines 358-363 is also an empty body. These are documented placeholders, but they add per-event work and dead code. The test "makes a subscription callback fired after teardown inert" in `src/test/use-chart-provider.errors.test.tsx` asserts that `getVisibleRange` was not called. That passes whether or not the guard exists, because the handler never calls anything. Either defer the subscriptions until a consumer exists, or test the disposer lifecycle through real handler behavior.

findings.title: Failed create is followed by a spurious second error from teardown
findings.description: If `provider.create()` throws, for example because `createChart` throws, `LightweightChartsProvider.chart` is still null. `src/chart/providers/lightweight-charts-provider.ts:67-70` shows `destroy()` calls `assertReady()`, which throws. The shared `teardown` then logs a misleading "provider teardown failed" error right after the real "create failed" one. The spy never throws from `destroy`, so the unit tests miss this. Consider tracking whether `create` succeeded and skipping `destroy` when it did not.

findings.title: `readChartStyle` silently falls back to library defaults
findings.description: `CLAUDE.md` says "Never use silent fallback values". When a theme token resolves empty, it is dropped without any signal. If all three are empty the function returns `undefined`, and a partial miss leaves that color at the library default. A renamed token would therefore turn the chart white with no error. The e2e test catches the case where `--color-surface` is missing. A grid or text token that goes missing is not caught. Log or throw on a missing token. At minimum, test `readChartStyle` directly, since there is no unit test for it.

findings.title: Stale and misplaced comments in the hook, and the smoke spec names the wrong file
findings.description:
- The header refers to "task 14" and a build-up "across tasks 8/10/12/14", which is process history.
- The `teardown` comment says subscriptions "join here in task 12", but they already do.
- The "The forwarding facade…" comment block sits above the `series` memo instead of the `chart` memo it describes.
- In `e2e/smoke.spec.ts:10` the comment says "The chart itself is asserted in chart-render.spec.ts". That spec covers the harness route. The product chart is covered by `chart-live.spec.ts`.

findings.title: Initial size uses the border box, later resizes use the content box
findings.description: The initial size comes from `getBoundingClientRect()`, which includes the container's 1px border. Observer updates use `contentRect`, which excludes it. The chart is therefore 2px oversized until the observer's first callback corrects it, and the e2e check only requires more than 50% of the container width, so it would not catch this. Using one measurement source would remove the inconsistency.

findings.title: Harness gate relies on a manual bundle check
findings.description: The mode strings `'e2e'` and `'development'` are written inline, and `playwright.config.ts` repeats `e2e`. That is a deliberate trade-off to keep the tree-shaking working, and the comment explains it. The guarantee that production excludes the harness was verified by hand. A small build-output check, such as grepping the production bundle for `__chart-harness` in CI, would protect it from regressions. The `react-hooks/refs` suppression in `eslint.config.js` is scoped to one file and documented, which is acceptable.

findings.title: Lifecycle, error funnel and test support design
findings.description:
- The single `runGuarded` funnel, the disposed flag, and the unsubscribe → disconnect → destroy teardown order are coherent.
- The `ready`/`error` state is held as one unit, and each disposer is pushed on its own so a mid-setup throw does not leak the first.
- The lifecycle facade subset deliberately omits `create` and `destroy`.
- The spy and `renderWithContexts` helpers keep the four hook suites consistent.
- `getCapability` keeps its generic through the facade.
- The removal of `WorkspaceRoute` leaves no dangling references.
